variants.title: From the office to the kitchen
variants.text:
Five years ago, Carla Rossi was working as an accountant in a big London bank. She earned a good salary, but she wasn't happy. "I had been sitting in front of a computer for ten years," she says, "and I felt that life was passing me by."

Everything changed one Sunday in 2019. Carla had baked a cake for a friend's birthday, and one of the guests asked if she could make one for her wedding. "I said yes before I had time to think," she laughs.

Two years later she left the bank and opened a small bakery in Bristol. Since then, she has made more than three thousand cakes, and she has never regretted her decision. However, it hasn't always been easy. "In the first year I worked seven days a week, and I didn't earn much. Even now, if I had a free day, I'd probably spend it sleeping!"

Her advice for anyone who wants to change careers? "Don't wait for the perfect moment. It doesn't exist. Start small: bake at the weekends and keep your job until you're sure."

options: She has made more than 3,000 cakes.

She has gone back to the bank.

items.prompt: What does Carla say about her new life?
options: It's better, but it has been hard work.
It's easier than her old job.

items.prompt: What would Carla do with a free day?
What can we say about Carla?

variants.title: Across Ireland on foot
variants.text:
Last summer, Liam Byrne, a retired teacher from Dublin, walked from one side of Ireland to the other. He had been planning the trip for years, but he had never had enough time while he was working.

"I left Dublin on the first of June," he explains. "Twenty-three days later, I arrived in Galway. My feet were in a terrible state, but I was the happiest man in Ireland!"

Since then, Liam has written a short book about the journey, and he has given all the money from it to a children's hospital. "People have been incredibly generous," he says. "So far, the book has raised twelve thousand euros."

Although he is sixty, Liam is already planning his next adventure. "If I were twenty years younger, I'd walk across Spain. But maybe I'll just do the Camino de Santiago. That's why I've started learning Spanish!"

He says walking alone was the best part. "When you walk for eight hours a day, you have time to think. I had been teaching for thirty-five years and I had never stopped to think about my own life."

options: Liam has given it to a hospital.

dialogue.speaker: Ollie
dialogue.text: Right, dinner's ready. It's a Spanish tortilla. My first one!

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.text: Wow, it smells great. By the way, Sam called this afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Ollie
dialogue.text: Oh yeah? How's London?

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.text: He said they had finished three songs already. And the producer loves them.

dialogue.speaker: Ollie
dialogue.text: That's brilliant. When's the album coming out?

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.text: In the spring, I think. Anyway, let me try this. Mmm, it's better than my mum's!

dialogue.speaker: Ollie
dialogue.text: Really? My grandmother used to cook for twelve people every Sunday. She would let me help her in the kitchen.

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.text: So that's how you became a chef!

dialogue.speaker: Ollie
dialogue.text: Exactly. So, what are you doing this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.text: Daniel and I are going to a gig on Saturday. Do you want to come?

dialogue.speaker: Ollie
dialogue.text: I'd love to, but I'm working. Actually, I always work on Saturdays. Restaurant life!

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.text: Never mind, next time. And don't worry about the washing-up. I'll do it.

dialogue.speaker: Javi
dialogue.text: Daniel! How's it going?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel

dialogue.speaker: Javi
